title: Affinities of one group to another are usually general, not to any single species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Affinities of one group to another are usually general, not to any single species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When a member of one group shows a real affinity to a quite distinct group, the affinity is usually general rather than to any particular species, because it retains characters of an ancient common progenitor of both groups.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: when a member belonging to one group of animals exhibits an affinity to a quite distinct group, this affinity in most cases is general and not special

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “Affinities, general, complex and radiating”. Scope: members of distinct orders or families of animals and plants that show cross-group affinities

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ancestral character reconstruction can test specific examples. The qualitative categories and lack of a comprehensive affinity dataset prevent a general resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Code claimed cross-group morphological affinities and test whether each character maps broadly near the common ancestor of both groups rather than uniquely linking particular terminal species. A predominance of ancestral, broadly distributed characters supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available matrices are not a representative sample of asserted cross-group affinities.

Affinity, general and special need expert coding.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Character mapping can separate a general resemblance to a group from a special resemblance to one species, which is the empirical contrast in the sentence. The required matrices exist for scattered taxa rather than for every cross-group affinity Darwin had in mind. Months of character coding would still leave a moderate risk that the result restates how the characters were chosen.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: When a species shares characters with a distant group, map those characters on an independent tree and ask whether they are ancestral for the distant group or shared uniquely with one of its species. The claim is confirmed if such cross-group similarities are usually general plesiomorphies, and refuted if they usually match derived characters of a single species.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Pre-cladistic 'affinity' mixes ancestral resemblance with convergence, so the characters to map are not uniquely defined.

The living members of a group are an incomplete sample of the ancient parent group whose characters the claim invokes.

Many matrices were assembled in order to resolve these same affinities, which makes the mapping partly circular.
